OpenRBI Vessel-RBI

Demonstration Risk-Based Inspection workspace for pressure vessel screening, calculation support and user-controlled RBI records. Engineering review remains required before any decision.

Overall process

Inspection / process data → OpenRBI vessel assessment → Engineering review & authorisation

Important Notice and Conditions of Use

OpenRBI — Important Notice and Conditions of Use

Please read before using OpenRBI.

OpenRBI is a free demonstration and proof-of-concept RBI workspace. It is not a production engineering system and does not provide engineering certification, regulatory approval, or certified assessments. You must independently verify all inputs and outputs before use.

Full notice and conditions of use

1. Demonstration and Proof-of-Concept Website

OpenRBI is a free, user-operated demonstration and proof-of-concept website, including for training purposes. It has been developed to illustrate a transparent, traceable, and reviewable approach to Risk-Based Inspection (RBI) calculations and documentation.

OpenRBI provides a calculation and record-management workspace for screening, training, education, calculation support, evaluation, discussion, and the preparation of user-controlled RBI calculation records.

OpenRBI is not a production engineering system. It must not be used as the sole basis for engineering decisions, inspection planning, inspection interval extension, inspection deferral, fitness-for-service assessment, regulatory compliance decisions, maintenance deferral, risk acceptance, safety-critical decisions, plant operation, regulatory submissions, or authorisation for continued operation.

A complete, deployable RBI system would require extensive customisation to national, local, and customer requirements — including codes, standards, data libraries, workflows, approvals, and record-keeping — before it could be considered fit for operational or decision-making use in any practical sense.

2. No Engineering Approval or Certification

OpenRBI exports user-generated RBI calculation records only. It does not issue approved, certified, or regulator-accepted RBI assessments.

OpenRBI does not provide engineering certification, regulatory approval, statutory inspection approval, fitness-for-service approval, inspection interval approval, inspection deferral approval, plant safety assurance, or any other formal engineering approval.

Engineering approval by OpenRBI is not provided. Regulatory approval is not provided. No certification status is conferred by OpenRBI.

Access to or use of the website does not create a contract for professional engineering services, an engineer-client relationship, or any obligation to provide engineering advice, verification, certification, approval, maintenance, or ongoing support.

Any professional engineering service provided separately by an RPEQ engineer is a separate engagement and must be governed by its own written scope of services and formally issued deliverables.

3. User Responsibility and Competent Review

OpenRBI is intended for use only by suitably qualified and experienced personnel.

All calculations, inputs, assumptions, reference data, damage mechanisms, consequence assumptions, inspection history, inspection intervals, outputs, and conclusions must be independently checked by the user before use.

Any output must be reviewed by a competent engineer, Registered Professional Engineer of Queensland (RPEQ), certified inspector, owner-user representative, statutory authority, or other appropriately qualified person where required by applicable law, site rules, codes, standards, and jurisdictional requirements.

The user remains responsible for the final interpretation, acceptance, use, and implementation of any OpenRBI output.

4. Demonstration Data and Examples

Any pre-filled data, default values, sample records, demonstration examples, reference examples, and illustrative calculations are provided for demonstration purposes only.

They must not be treated as recommended values, site-specific values, approved values, or suitable values for any actual plant, equipment, facility, or inspection programme.

The user is responsible for replacing all example data with independently verified, site-specific information before any output is considered for further review.

5. Local Browser Processing and Data Control

OpenRBI operates within the user’s web browser. It does not require a login, user account, or registration.

User-selected files, equipment data, inspection data, calculation records, and exported reports are processed locally within the browser. The OpenRBI application does not upload, transmit, receive, store, or retain the contents of user-selected files or user-generated RBI calculation records.

OpenRBI does not use server-side storage, databases, external application programming interfaces, analytics scripts, third-party trackers, or data-upload services.

The website is not an archival storage service. Users remain responsible for retaining their own master copies of all source files, exported files, PDF reports, calculation records, and supporting documents.

6. Website Updates, Version Control and Compatibility

OpenRBI may be updated periodically. Updates may change the website layout, features, calculation methods, assumptions, default values, examples, documentation, file formats, or outputs.

Users are responsible for recording the OpenRBI version and date used for any retained calculation record. Users must independently verify outputs following any update.

No representation is made that files or outputs created using one version of OpenRBI will remain identical to, or fully compatible with, a later version.

7. Website Availability and Downtime

The OpenRBI website may be unavailable from time to time due to maintenance, updates, technical issues, or other downtime.

Continuous access is not guaranteed. The website, any feature, and the service itself may be changed, suspended, or discontinued at any time without notice.

Users must not rely on the website as the sole repository for any file, calculation record, or supporting document.

8. Exported PDF Reports and Calculation Records

Any PDF report or calculation record exported from OpenRBI is a user-generated calculation record.

It is not an engineering certificate, statutory inspection certificate, fitness-for-service approval, inspection deferral approval, regulatory compliance certificate, or plant safety assurance document.

Review status: requires competent review before use.

9. Standards, Codes and Recommended Practices

OpenRBI supports API 580 and industry screening-style RBI workflows but does not claim to replace competent engineering review, statutory inspection, professional judgement, site procedures, owner-user responsibility, or regulatory approval.

Any reference to standards, codes, or recommended practices is provided for calculation support and workflow alignment only. It is not a statement of compliance, certification, or approval.

10. Limitations of Responsibility

To the maximum extent permitted by law, no responsibility is accepted for loss arising from reliance on the website, its calculations, its outputs, user-generated files, inaccurate or incomplete input data, unverified assumptions, changes to calculations or file formats, incompatibility between versions, modification by others, loss of access, interruption of service, or discontinuation of the website.

Users are responsible for satisfying themselves that any calculation record, output, or file is suitable for their intended purpose and for obtaining any required independent professional review, statutory approval, or authorisation before use.

11. Acceptance

By accessing or using OpenRBI, the user acknowledges that the website is a free demonstration and proof-of-concept workspace only and accepts responsibility for independently reviewing and verifying any information, calculation, output, or file generated through its use.

M0 — Users Data
How to use Module 0 — click to open

M0 holds your (the user) reference libraries, for this RBI file (location, chemicals, materials, GFF, risk matrix, planning, and more). Edit tables here, then refresh so M1–M8 use the latest data.

  1. Document title / date — Identify this Users Data document.
  2. Edit library sections (M0.1–M0.17) — Update Location, Chemical, Materials, Damage, Risk matrix, GFF, Planning, Inspection methods, etc.
  3. Load / Save document — Use Load document / Save document for a standalone M0 JSON, separate from the vessel file if needed.
  4. Refresh — Click Refresh (or the module refresh icon) after edits so Libraries and later modules pick up changes.

Keep Location and Materials aligned with what you will select in M1. Risk matrix and planning tables drive M6–M7.

M0.1 — Location
M0.2 — Chemical

Edit the table below. Once loaded in Engine 3 (Load Rules JSON or Acid in Libraries), acid fluid properties are used for Industry screening acid release and consequence analysis.

M0.5 — Materials

Edit the table below. Once loaded in Engine 3 (Load Rules JSON or Materials in Libraries), material specs and allowable stress are used in M5 Damage (min wall calculations) and material selection.

M0.6 — Damage

Edit the table below. Once loaded in Engine 3 (Load Rules JSON or Damage in Libraries), the mechanism library drives M5 Damage screening, cracking/other mechanism lists, and inspection/definition lookups.

M0.7 — Risk consequences

Edit the table below. Once loaded in Engine 3 (Load Rules JSON or Risk consequences in Libraries), consequence dimensions and score options are used in M6 Risk for CoF scoring and probability bands.

M0.8 — Risk Matrix

Edit the table below. Once loaded in Engine 3 (Load Rules JSON or Risk Matrix in Libraries), the matrix drives M6 Risk (PoF × CoF, risk level, planning). Cell highlight colors are applied in M6 when you leave M0 (switch to M1–M9) or use Save combined CSV (full export), which pushes this snapshot into REF so the live matrix can read cells and colors.

M0.9 — Area Affected

Edit the table below. Once loaded in Engine 3 (Load Rules JSON or Area Affected in Libraries), area bands are used in M6 Risk for consequence and release area mapping.

M0.10 — GFF (generic failure frequency)

Edit the table below. Once loaded in Engine 3, GFF (generic failure frequency) (Table 3.1, failures/yr) is used with calculated Df,thin in M3 min-wall GFF method and M6 PoF (GFF (generic failure frequency) × FMS (management systems factor) × Df,thin (damage factor)).

M0.11 — PoF Mapping

Edit the table below. Once loaded in Engine 3 (Load Rules JSON or PoF Mapping in Libraries), numeric bands map working PoF (GFF (generic failure frequency) × FMS (management systems factor) × DF (damage factor)) to a 1–5 score in M6 Risk; the M6 PoF tab shows the GFF (generic failure frequency)/FMS (management systems factor)/DF (damage factor) breakdown and per-row mapped bands for min-wall calcs.

M0.12 — PoF Matrix score

Edit the table below. CoF matrix column letters (A–E) and the M6 Driving consequence dropdown labels (1–5 with comment text) are taken from this table once loaded in Engine 3 or from M0 RBI Data.

M0.13 — Half remaining life

Edit the table below. Once loaded in Engine 3 (Load Rules JSON or Half remaining life in Libraries), numeric bands use the same columns as PoF Mapping — min, max, score, and label. Enter min / max as half-life in years (same units as the M3 min-wall 1/2 life (yrs) result). Shorter half-life → higher PoF score (5 = most urgent). Default bands match built-in M3 tiers: <2 yr→5, 2–6→4, 6–10→3, >10–16→2, >16 yr→1.

Edit the table below. Once loaded in Engine 3 (Load Rules JSON or Management Score in Libraries), the questionnaire and FMS (management systems factor) are used with M3 GFF (generic failure frequency) and in M6 PoF (GFF (generic failure frequency) × FMS (management systems factor) × DF (damage factor)).

M0.16 — Planning

Edit the table below. Once loaded in Engine 3 (Load Rules JSON or Planning in Libraries), risk-cell-to-frequency mapping is used in M7 Planning to suggest inspection intervals from risk score.

Module 1 — Asset register
How to use Module 1 — click to open

Record the vessel identity, location, design and operating data used by later modules (M2–M7). Complete the sections in order. Save with the global save control when you finish.

  1. M1.1 Location — Choose Site, Unit / Area, and System from the locked M0 Location list only. Set whether the item is in a bunded area.
  2. M1.2 Basic Info — Enter tag, name, description, date vessel new, insulation, and heat treatment. Tag and name appear in the header and report.
  3. M1.3 Design Conditions — Enter design temperature, design pressure (gauge), shell nominal thickness, and corrosion allowance (from the vessel design / nameplate data).
  4. M1.4 Operating Conditions — Enter typical operating temperature and pressure (gauge), liquid level (%), and total vessel volume (L). Volume and level feed release / inventory calculations in M3.
  5. M1.5 Component design — Add shell, heads, nozzles, and other components. Materials come from the M0 Materials library. These rows feed M5 min-wall and damage calculations.
  6. M1.6 Design reports — Link design documents (name, URL, description). Use Open to open a link in a new tab.
  7. M1.7 / M1.8 Notes — Optional design notes and additional notes (text, links, images). Included in the printed module / report where applicable.

Use the refresh icon on the module title to re-apply M0 libraries after Location or Materials changes in M0. Pressures in M1 are gauge; later release maths convert to absolute where required.

M1.1 — Location

Select from the locked M0 Location master list only. Values not in that list are left blank with a warning. Choose Site first, then Unit / Area, then System.

M1.2 — Basic Info

Identify the vessel. Date vessel new is used as the age start date in damage calculations (M5). Insulation and heat treatment support damage screening.

M1.3 — Design Conditions

Enter values from the design code / nameplate (e.g. ASME VIII). Pressure is gauge (MPa). These values are shown or inherited in M2–M7.

M1.4 — Operating Conditions

Typical operating values for release scenarios. Pressure is gauge. Vessel % liquid level and Total volume support inventory and time-to-empty in M3.

M1.5 — Component design

Register vessel components. Material options come from the M0 Materials library. Use the delete icon to remove a row, + on a row to insert below it, or + Add row at the end.

Actions Component Internal size (mm) Material Nominal thickness (mm)
M1.6 — Design reports

Link design documents for this vessel. Use Open to launch a URL in a new tab. Use delete to remove a row, + on a row to insert below it, or + Add row at the end.

Module 2 — Level 1 CoF analysis

How to use Module 2 — click to open

Build the Level 1 consequence-of-failure analysis: chemistry mixtures, release source terms, detection/isolation, screening areas, aggregation, and owner CoF.

  1. M2.1–M2.4 Chemistry — Enter flammable, toxic, acid, and inert compositions (mole %). Properties come from M0 chemical libraries.
  2. M2.5 Fluid & conditions — Confirm representative fluid, phase, MW, density, and AIT (from M2/M3).
  3. M2.6 Holes & inventory — Review hole sizes and Wₙ from M3; set available inventory mass.
  4. M2.7 Detection / isolation — Choose detection and isolation classes; calculate source term (rateₙ / massₙ).
  5. M2.8–M2.11 Areas, aggregation, CoF, driving — Enter or pull consequence areas, aggregate models, set owner CoF and driving consequence.
  6. M2.12 Notes — Optional analysis notes.

Complete M1 first and run M3 Calculate All Holes so release rates and inventory can flow into M2.5–M2.7. With DP # on, fields under M2.7 are numbered M2.71, M2.72…

Module 3 — Release Rate Estimation

Inherited from M2 — Chemistry Name —
How to use Module 3 — click to open

Estimate release rates for the four standard hole sizes. Results feed M2 Level 1 CoF and downstream consequence work.

  1. M3.1 Representative fluid — Select the fluid (usually from M2).
  2. M3.2 Release inputs — Set phase, pressure (from M1 gauge options), back pressure, temperature, Cd, and gas k if needed. Vessel volume comes from M1.
  3. M3.3 Results — Click Calculate All Holes to get Wₙ, mass, and continuous/instant classification.
  4. M3.4 SEA — Optional specialist engineering assessment notes/links.

M1 pressures are gauge; release maths use absolute where required. Save M3 after calculating so M2 can refresh rates.

Module 5 — Damage mechanism

from M1 Shell Nominal Thickness (mm) — · from M1 Design Pressure (MPa) GAUGE — · from M1 Shell Corrosion Allowance (mm) —
How to use Module 5 — click to open

Screen and analyse damage mechanisms: equipment GFF baseline, thinning (min wall), cracking, other damage, and related notes.

  1. M5.1 Equipment GFF — Select the M0 GFF row and confirm management / FMS baseline.
  2. M5.2 Thinning — Component min-wall and thinning DF steps (materials and sizes from M1).
  3. Further M5 sections — Complete cracking, other mechanisms, inspections, and notes as applicable.
  4. Consequence models — Build / refresh consequence models where prompted so M6 can read areas.

Design pressure, nominal thickness, corrosion allowance, and date vessel new come from M1. Refresh after M0/M1 changes.

M5.1 — Equipment GFF (generic failure frequency)

Set the equipment baseline before damage mechanisms: choose the M0 GFF (generic failure frequency) row. The right-hand readouts show GFF total, your M0 Management score / FMS, and GFF total × FMS (baseline before DF). Each damage-mechanism tab then scales PoF with DF only. Module 3 locks the release scenario hole for consequence.

M5.2 — Thinning
ASME VIII-1 formulas & references
RBI/FFS: t_min = pressure thickness only (CA tracked separately as REM. CA). FFS = max(Absolute Minimum Wall, t_min) per ASME VIII-1 UG-16.2 / component selection. Design pressure, nominal thickness, and corrosion allowance are taken from Module 1 (Asset register).
Shell UG-27(c): t = PR/(SE − 0.6P)  ·  factor 0.6
2:1 Ellipsoidal UG-32(c): t = PDK/(2SE − 0.2P), K=1  ·  factor 0.2
Torispherical UG-32(d): t = PLM/(2SE − 0.2P), M from Table 1-4.2  ·  factor 0.2
Hemispherical UG-32(e): t = PL/(2SE − 0.2P)  ·  factor 0.2
Conical UG-32(f): t = PD/(2SE − 0.2P)cos(α)  ·  factor 0.2
Toriconical UG-32(g): knuckle per 1-4(d)(3)  ·  factor 0.2
Flat head / blind flange UG-34: t = d√(CP/SE), C from Fig. UG-34  ·  C factor
Nozzle neck UG-27(c): t = PR/(SE − 0.6P)  ·  factor 0.6, small-opening rules
Large opening UG-36/37: neck per UG-27; reinforcement per UG-37  ·  Special

Rows from M5 Damage appear automatically. Use Add row for a manual entry, or duplicate an existing row with the replicate icon. Drag column edges to resize (like Excel). Module 8 — Report

How to use Module 8 — click to open

Produce a consolidated report from the completed analysis modules.

  1. Produce report — Click to generate the report body from saved M1–M7 data and M4 history.
  2. Review — Scroll the report content; use Print on the module title to print.
  3. Refresh — Re-apply M0 and reload after upstream edits, then Produce report again.

The report stays blank until you click Produce report. Ensure modules are saved first.

Click Produce report to generate the report. Modules M1–M8 and M8 history.
